newsitem.title: USA: U.S. watchdog says media covers easy news.
newsitem.headline: U.S. watchdog says media covers easy news.

text.p: A media watchdog Friday criticised mainstream media for carrying too many stories about fast-food prices, new products and celebrities instead of covering issues like health care and welfare reform.
"We hear all about 'the burger wars' and Windows 95," said Laura Flanders of Fairness & Accuracy in Reporting (FAIR), a New York-based media monitoring group.
But newspapers and television have not provided enough analysis of the long-term effects of welfare reform, changes in health care or international trade agreements, she said.
In a speech to the City Club of Cleveland, a free-speech forum, Flanders said the views of minorities, women, the poor and the powerless have been under-reported.

Media outlets owned by large corporations often focus on news that they believe will attract the broadest audience for their advertisers, and reporters and editors shy away from complex issues to report events with visual impact such as celebrity murder trials, she said.
